problem_type: PowerShell scenario subprocesses must have explicit success and visible failure at a shared execution boundary
symptom: Windows run 41008253991: A1-A13 exit during resetMachine; only CLIXML progress is visible and CX1-CX3 are correctly NOT RED.
direct_cause: resetMachine ends with Remove-Item on absent work/s under script-level SilentlyContinue. Implicit powershell.exe exit follows false $?; helper prefers progress-only stderr over stdout.
class_root: No common contract for terminating errors, explicit exit, and diagnostic capture across inline, -File watcher and spawned lock scripts.
affected_population: All installer scenarios on clean Windows runners
Missing attribute targets, failed registry writes, watcher and lock helper failures
entry_points: Ten synchronous powershell calls (eleven textual matches including definition)

external_sources.purpose: Explicit exit required rather than last-command $? semantics.

invariants: All scripts run through Stop/try/catch, stdout marker plus message and position, exit 0/1.
File cleanup uses fs.rmSync recursive force, registry absent paths guarded by Test-Path.
Progress is never reported as error text; asynchronous process failures cannot produce a passing scenario.

door_reduction.why_not: powershell owns platform calls, resetMachine owns scenario isolation, attributesOf owns attribute reads; separate responsibilities converge at one subprocess boundary.

generality_proof: Common PS1 boundary is invoked by encoded inline scripts and dot-sourced by the -File watcher. Sync and async diagnostics share one XML parser. Node owns filesystem deletion. No caller relies on final $? or script-level error suppression.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Stop, explicit exit and stdout failure diagnostics.
Keep both streams and process failure; remove progress through XML parsing.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Get-Item inherits Stop; missing files terminate rather than silently shortening JSON.
New-ItemProperty inherits Stop; failures reach shared catch with position.
Dot sources shared PS1; Node captures streams and validates lifecycle.
Shared encoded script and captured spawn errors; intentional kill distinguished from premature exit.

recurrence.reason: Every scenario and future clean Windows run can reach the same implicit exit and swallowed-error mechanism.
same_class_scan: rg powershell/Remove-Item/EncodedCommand/-File across tests/installer: ten synchronous calls plus watcher and lock helper
Reviewed registryEntries, pendingRecordExists, setRegistryValue, processesUnder, attributesOf, isElevated, shortcutPaths, resetMachine, expectNoRegistration, main Documents resolver.

prevention.invariant: Explicit successful exit or caught error with original message and position, shared by every script.
prevention.failure_mode: Node throws visible diagnostic and scenario stays red.
prevention.strategy: Replace implicit shell completion with one wrapper, use existing xmldom parser, delete PowerShell file cleanup and script-level suppression.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove raw encoded execution, ignored watcher output, implicit success and PowerShell filesystem deletion in same change.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Windows PowerShell 5.1 is built into runner; no runtime installation needed. Existing @xmldom/xmldom 0.9.12 handles XML.
dependency_lifecycle.target: Supported Windows PowerShell runtime and existing XML parser
exit_criteria: Runtime/parser upgrades must pass static and CLIXML regression tests plus Windows A1-A13 and CX1-CX3.

migration: No user state migration; CI harness only. Existing scenarios and installer logic unchanged.
residual_risks: Mac has no PowerShell: static and diagnostic parser tests do not execute registry, NTFS, UAC or installer behavior. Windows loop is required.
